briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 17, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Materialized Threats
sections.content: Recent reports clearly demonstrate the intensifying impacts of climate change. While 17th-century glacial lake outbursts were attributed to sunspots, today's glacial lake outbursts are now linked to global warming [4]. Vietnam has released its 2025 climate change scenario, warning of increased risks of heatwaves, extreme rainfall, and floods [6], and due to the El Niño phenomenon, California is already experiencing a preview of climate change's grim future [28]. These climate changes pose severe threats across entire ecosystems, such as the destruction of Vietnamese spiny toad habitats [45], and are materializing globally, including the disappearance of Slovenia's last glacier [46]. Furthermore, the UN climate panel's failure to agree on a date for global warming updates [40] suggests difficulties in international cooperation for addressing the climate crisis.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts for Climate Change Adaptation and Carbon Neutrality Implementation
sections.content: Despite the threats of climate change, various adaptation and carbon neutrality efforts are continuing both domestically and internationally. Domestically, Yecheon Nonghyup is sharing climate change response strategies through ginger cultivation technology education [1], and the Rural Development Administration (RDA) is supporting beekeeping farmers' winter preparations, enhancing the agricultural sector's adaptability to changing climates [2]. Nexmore Systems is promoting citizen safety by developing climate safety services using heatwave maps [5], and the Korea National Arboretum is discussing directions for creating future value tailored to climate change [3], among other sectors actively seeking practical countermeasures. In the field of carbon neutrality, Cheonan City is exploring citizen-participatory policies and holding forums, emphasizing 'action' [7, 9, 11, 14], and Seoul City has completed the third-year evaluation of its carbon neutrality projects in the building sector [10]. Furthermore, 'Academy Namu' has officially launched with the goal of moving beyond carbon neutrality declarations to implementation [12], and Incheon's Jemulpo District's Wolmi Park and Jorim Elementary School are spreading carbon neutrality practices through ecological environment experiences and sweet potato harvesting in community gardens [8, 13]. Internationally, as demand for carbon neutrality increases in global supply chains, rooftop solar panel installation is becoming essential for export companies [16, 26].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Technology Innovation Trends
sections.content: Positive developments continue in the renewable energy sector, which is central to the future energy transition. The International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) projects that 38.2 TW of renewable energy will be needed by 2050, with solar and wind power accounting for over 80% of this [17]. In line with this trend, the '2026 Asia-Pacific Renewable Energy Matching Forum' is scheduled to be held in Seoul [18], and the popularization of renewable energy is accelerating, with even local cafes now able to purchase renewable energy through a 'subscription' model, lowering accessibility barriers [19]. Furthermore, investments are active, with Toho Gas, for example, investing in the Goldfinch Solar Power Project in Texas, USA [21], and Jeollabuk-do Province is also promoting the expansion of household balcony solar power systems [25]. Driven by the increasing demand for renewable energy, related industrial ecosystems are also thriving, with the surge arrester cartridge component market and the high-voltage ceramic zinc oxide surge arrester market projected to grow at an average annual rate of 5.8% until 2035 [22, 23]. Concurrently, KEPCO KDN is supplying cryptographic modules to strengthen the cybersecurity of private solar power generation [24], and the University at Buffalo is installing weather observatories for climate change research [34], demonstrating continuous technological advancement and expansion of research infrastructure.

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Call for Climate Action and Challenges
sections.content: The international community is calling for action to address climate change while also facing numerous challenges. Climate change is acting as a powerful force driving migration [27], and discussions continue regarding its ambiguous costs [29], with warnings emerging that even the insurance industry may not be able to protect us from climate change risks [37]. Meanwhile, equity issues concerning who shapes climate science have been raised with the IPCC [38], and oil companies are facing climate change-related lawsuits [36]. Amidst these circumstances, messages such as 'Earth for the Future: Restoring Trust Through Climate Action' [39] and the COP31 Youth Declaration [48] emphasize the importance of climate action. On a positive note, a Tanzanian innovator won the UN Climate Change AI Climate Action Award in 2026 [49], and international efforts are also underway, with approximately 58% of countries worldwide announcing new pledges to address nature loss at COP17 [52].

briefing.closing: In today's briefing, we examined the materialized threats of the climate crisis, as well as various domestic and international efforts and innovations to overcome them. Continued international cooperation, technological development, and active participation from civil society will be key to overcoming the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
